---
title: "Buckling-Constrained Truss Optimization with SDP Constraints"
toc: true
---

## Description

This tutorial demonstrates buckling-constrained topology optimization on a
truss structure. The goal is to minimize compliance while ensuring the
combined stiffness matrix `K + c·Kσ` remains positive semidefinite — i.e.,
the structure does not buckle under the applied load scaled by buckling
factor `c`.

We use differentiable building blocks (`ElementKFun`, `AssembleKFun`,
`TrussElementKσFun`, `apply_boundary_with_zerodiag!`, `apply_boundary_with_meandiag!`)
and enforce the PSD constraint via semidefinite programming (SDP) using
NonconvexSemidefinite.jl with an IPM barrier method.

## Setup

```{julia}
#| output: false
using TopOpt, LinearAlgebra, Zygote
using Nonconvex, NonconvexSemidefinite, NonconvexIpopt
using WGLMakie
WGLMakie.activate!(; resize_to=:parent)
using Bonito
if haskey(ENV, "QUARTO_PROJECT_DIR")
    Bonito.Page(exportable=true, offline=true)
else
    Bonito.browser_display()
end
display_app(app) = display(app)
```

`WGLMakie.activate!(; resize_to=:parent)` selects the browser renderer and fills the Quarto output column. `Bonito.Page(exportable=true, offline=true)` embeds the assets needed by `visualize(...; static=true)` in the Quarto output, so the visualization does not require a running Julia process.

## Load Truss Geometry

Download the truss geometry file: [tim_2d.json](tim_2d.json).

```{julia}
#| output: false
ndim = 2
node_points, elements, _, _, fixities, load_cases = load_truss_json(
    joinpath(@__DIR__, "tim_$(ndim)d.json")
)
ndim, nnodes, ncells = length(node_points[1]), length(node_points), length(elements)
loads = load_cases["0"]

# Override material and cross-section: a large area (A=800) makes the
# stiffness matrix K dominate the geometric stiffness Kσ, so the initial
# all-solid design is stable (K + c·Kσ ≻ 0) while still allowing the
# compliance-only optimum to go unstable.
mats = TrussFEAMaterial(1.0, 0.3)
crosssecs = TrussFEACrossSec(800.0)

problem = TrussProblem(
    node_points, elements, loads, fixities, mats, crosssecs
)
```

## Parameter Settings

```{julia}
#| output: false
xmin = 0.0001   # minimum density
p = 1.0         # SIMP penalty exponent
V = 0.5         # volume fraction
x0 = fill(1.0, ncells)  # initial design (all solid)
```

## FEA Solver and Buckling Helpers

```{julia}
#| output: false
solver = FEASolver(DirectSolver, problem; xmin=xmin)
ch = problem.ch

comp = ComplianceFun(solver)
dp = DisplacementFun(solver)
assemble_k = AssembleKFun(problem)
element_k = ElementKFun(solver)
truss_element_kσ = TrussElementKσFun(problem, solver)
```

Five differentiable building blocks:

1. **ComplianceFun** — objective to minimize
2. **DisplacementFun** — solves `K·u = f` for displacements
3. **ElementKFun** — per-element stiffness matrices
4. **AssembleKFun** — assembles global sparse matrix
5. **TrussElementKσFun** — geometric (stress) stiffness matrices

## Buckling Constraint Function

```{julia}
#| output: false
c = 1.0  # buckling load multiplier — large enough that the constraint binds

function buckling_matrix_constr(x)
    xd = PseudoDensities(x)
    u = dp(xd)
    Kes = element_k(xd)
    K = assemble_k(Kes)
    K = apply_boundary_with_meandiag!(K, ch)
    Kσs = truss_element_kσ(u, xd)
    Kσ = assemble_k(Kσs)
    Kσ = apply_boundary_with_zerodiag!(Kσ, ch)
    return Array(K + c * Kσ)
end
```

The constraint returns the combined matrix `K + c·Kσ` which must be PSD
(all eigenvalues ≥ 0).

## Check Initial Design

```{julia}
#| output: true
S0 = buckling_matrix_constr(x0)
println("Initial design minimum eigenvalue: $(minimum(eigen(S0).values))")
```

The initial all-solid design should have positive eigenvalues (stable).

## Volume Constraint

```{julia}
#| output: false
vol_constr(x) = sum(x) / length(x) - V
```

## Compliance-Only Optimization (Baseline)

```{julia}
#| output: true
obj = x -> comp(PseudoDensities(x))

model = Model(obj)
addvar!(model, zeros(length(x0)), ones(length(x0)))
add_ineq_constraint!(model, vol_constr)

alg = MMA87()
options = MMAOptions(; maxiter=200, tol=Tolerance(; kkt=1e-4))
r1 = optimize(model, alg, x0; options=options)

println("ComplianceFun-only result:")
println("  obj = $(obj(r1.minimizer))")
println("  vol = $(vol_constr(r1.minimizer))")
```

This baseline ignores buckling — the result may be unstable.

## Add Buckling SDP Constraint

```{julia}
#| output: true
# Add semidefinite constraint: K + c·Kσ ≽ 0
add_sd_constraint!(model, buckling_matrix_constr)

alg2 = SDPBarrierAlg(; sub_alg=IpoptAlg())
options2 = SDPBarrierOptions(; 
    sub_options=IpoptOptions(; max_iter=200),
    keep_all=true
)
r2 = optimize(model, alg2, x0; options=options2)

println("Buckling-constrained result:")
println("  obj = $(obj(r2.minimizer))")
println("  vol = $(vol_constr(r2.minimizer))")
```

The `SDPBarrierAlg` uses an interior-point method with log-barrier for PSD
constraints. IPOPT solves the continuous subproblems.

## Check Stability

```{julia}
#| output: true
S1 = buckling_matrix_constr(r1.minimizer)
S2 = buckling_matrix_constr(r2.minimizer)

ev1 = eigen(S1).values
ev2 = eigen(S2).values

println("ComplianceFun-only min eigenvalue: $(minimum(ev1))")
println("Buckling-constrained min eigenvalue: $(minimum(ev2))")
println("Design is stable: $(minimum(ev2) ≥ -1e-6)")
```

The buckling-constrained design should have non-negative eigenvalues
(stable under load), while the compliance-only design may have negative
eigenvalues (unstable).

## Visualization

```{julia}
#| label: fig-buckling
#| fig-cap: "Buckling-constrained truss design (top) vs compliance-only (bottom)"
using Makie, WGLMakie

fig1 = visualize(problem; static=true, u=solver.u, topology=r1.minimizer, default_exagg_scale=0.0)
fig2 = visualize(problem; static=true, u=solver.u, topology=r2.minimizer, default_exagg_scale=0.0)
display_app(fig1)
display_app(fig2)
```

The buckling-constrained design typically shows thicker compression
members and more stable load paths compared to the compliance-only design.
